failure_patterns.pattern: answer_format: Answers were overexpanded relative to the concise requested form, adding a category noun or a clue-supplied qualifier.

rejected_edits.content: - Omit nonessential expansions even when they appear in a fuller contextual label: prefer a brand's short public name over its expanded company name, and omit middle initials or ordinal/rank modifiers unless the clue requests them or they are needed to disambiguate. Preserve the requested title or name itself.
rejected_edits.target: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity, using the concise form most directly supported by the clue and its evidence. Do not add an unnecessary corporate suffix or title subtitle, or repeat wording already supplied by the clue. For a person, use an explicitly supported full personal name rather than substituting a familiar nickname when the full name is the relevant answer. When a category is already specified, provide the distinguishing value rather than repeating the category.

rejected_edits.content: - When a clue asks about an abbreviation, expand it to the named feature rather than giving an associated mechanism or implementation detail. When a quotation visibly trails off, supply the next missing word if the clue asks for its continuation, rather than naming the work. For spoonerism clues, restore the intended phrase when that phrase is requested; do not substitute a person or other real-world referent.
rejected_edits.target: - Treat terse statements, quoted fragments, and incomplete phrases as information-seeking clues when appropriate. Infer the answer slot from the wording, then use the context to identify the entity or value that satisfies the clue.
